Food processor or small food chopper?

Match the bowl to your usual preparation

A 3.5-cup chopper and an 8- or 9-cup processor are different tools, even when both chop vegetables. Check usable capacity for liquids, the feed-tube opening and whether ingredients can be added during operation. For a family batch of slaw, slicing and shredding discs may be more useful than a small footprint. For a little sauce, a huge bowl can add unnecessary washing.

Compare the included blades and storage

List the tasks you need: chopping, slicing, shredding or dough. Confirm which approved accessories perform them and which are included with the exact model. Check lid interlocks and the availability of replacement bowls and pushers. Refurbished bundles can omit discs or storage boxes. A high wattage or large accessory count does not prove the machine is suited to every recipe.
